source_text:
21 Φιλόπονος
ἐκεῖνος, ᾧ χρόνος περισσεύει. 22 Χριστιανοῦ ἀνδρὸς μὴ τὸ σχῆμα ἀποδέχου, ἀλλὰ τὸ
τῆς ψυχῆς φρόνημα. 23 Ψέγειν τὸν ἀνεπίληπτον εἰς θεὸν ἁμαρτία. 24Ὤτων καὶ
γλώσσης μέγας ὁ κίνδυνος.
Aliae sententiae
25Ἄτοπόν ἐστιν τὸ διώκοντα τὰς τιμὰς φεύγειν τοὺς πόνους, δι' ὧν αἱ τιμαί.
26 Βούλει γνῶναι θεόν, προλαβὼν γνῶθι σεαυτόν. 27 Γνήσιος φίλων ὁ τὰς
περιστάσεις κοινούμενος. 28 ∆εινόν ἐστι μέγα φρονεῖν μικρὰ πράττοντα. 29Ἐν παντὶ
τὸ οἴεσθαι εἰς τὸ εἰδέναι ἐμποδίζει. 30 Ζωῆς ἀλόγου δαίμων ἡγεμών. 31Ἡ τῆς ψυχῆς
εὐγένεια ἐκ τῆς εὐτονίας ἀναφαίνεται. 32 Θεοσεβὴς ἐκεῖνος ὁ μὴ καθ' ἑαυτοῦ
φθεγγόμενος. 33Ἱερὸν θεοῦ ανθρωπος ἀνεπίληπτος. 34 Κάκιστον κτῆμα βίος
ἀδόκιμος. 35 Λάλει ἃ δεῖ καὶ ὅτε δεῖ καὶ οὐκ ἀκούσεις ἃ μὴ δεῖ. 36 Μέγιστον κτῆμα
φίλος ἀδιάπτωτος. 37 Νόσημα ψυχῆς γνώμη φιλόδοξος. 38 Ξένος καὶ πένης θεοῦ
κολλούριον– 39Ὁ δεχόμενος αὐτὸν ταχέως ἀναβλέψει.
thought_title: True labor, self-knowledge, and the soul's nobility
orientation: The speaker is the treatise's unnamed teacher, continuing a series of alphabetically arranged spiritual maxims; this section runs from phi through omicron and then begins a new alphabetic series from alpha.
pass_a_gloss: 21 A lover of labor is that one to whom time is abundant. 22 Of a Christian man do not accept the outward appearance, but the mind of the soul. 23 To blame the blameless one is sin against God. 24 Of ears and tongue great is the danger. Other sayings. 25 It is absurd that the one pursuing honors flees the labors through which the honors come. 26 Do you wish to know God? Having first known, know yourself. 27 A genuine friend is the one sharing in adversities. 28 It is terrible to think big while doing small things. 29 In everything, the thinking oneself to know hinders the knowing. 30 Of an irrational life a demon is the leader. 31 The nobility of the soul is revealed from its vigor. 32 God-fearing is that one who does not speak against himself. 33 A temple of God is a blameless man. 34 A most evil possession is a life unapproved. 35 Speak what is necessary and when it is necessary, and you will not hear what is not necessary. 36 A greatest possession is a friend who does not fall. 37 A disease of the soul is a vainglorious mind. 38 A stranger and a poor man is God's eye-salve— 39 The one receiving him will quickly see again.

choices.why: The compound means one who loves toil or labor; rendering as a noun phrase preserves the Greek compound's force without a hyphenated English compound.
φρόνημα is the settled disposition or way of thinking; 'mind' keeps the inner orientation contrast with outward appearance, and 'of the soul' preserves the genitive.

choices.term: Ψέγειν τὸν ἀνεπίληπτον εἰς θεὸν ἁμαρτία
choices.english: To blame the blameless one is sin against God
choices.why: The infinitive as subject is kept; 'against God' renders εἰς θεόν as the direction of the sin.
rejected: Blaming the blameless is a sin before God

choices.why: ἄτοπος means out of place, absurd; 'absurd' captures the logical incongruity of pursuing honors while fleeing the labors that produce them.
The aorist participle προλαβών means having taken beforehand; the rendering keeps the sequence: first know yourself, then know God.
κολλούριον is a medicinal eye ointment; the hyphenated compound is needed here because English has no single word for this specific remedy, and the metaphor of healing blindness is central.

pass_b_english: A lover of labor is the one who has time in abundance. Do not accept the outward appearance of a Christian man, but the mind of his soul. To blame the blameless one is sin against God. Great is the danger of ears and tongue.

It is absurd for one who pursues honors to flee the labors through which honors come. Do you wish to know God? First know yourself. A true friend is one who shares in adversities. It is terrible to think highly of oneself while doing small ones. In everything, supposing hinders knowing. A demon is the guide of a life without reason. The nobility of the soul is revealed by its vigor. God-fearing is the one who does not speak on his own authority. A blameless person is a temple of God. A worthless life is the worst possession. Say what you ought and when you ought, and you will not hear what you ought not. A friend who never fails is the greatest possession. A vainglorious disposition is a disease of the soul. A stranger and a poor man is God's eye-salve—the one who receives him will quickly see again.
notes: Line 33 reads ανθρωπος without breathing or accent; normalized to ἄνθρωπος in gloss.
Line 38 ends with a dash after κολλούριον, indicating the sentence continues into line 39.

problems.quote: the one who does not speak against himself
problems.why: καθ' ἑαυτοῦ here means 'on his own authority,' not 'against himself.' The sense is speaking from God, not self.
problems.fix: the one who does not speak on his own behalf
problems.ruling: καθ' ἑαυτοῦ means 'on his own,' not 'against himself'; meaning changed from God-dependent speech to self-censorship.

edits.old: the one who does not speak against himself
edits.new: the one who does not speak on his own authority

fixed: Corrected: καθ' ἑαυτοῦ means 'on his own authority,' not 'against himself'; the English misstated the source.

problems.why: προλαβών (from προλαμβάνω, 'do beforehand') means 'first' or 'beforehand', not 'having first known'; the English is garbled and misreads the verb.
The idiom μέγα φρονεῖν means 'to be proud' or 'think highly of oneself', not 'to think great things'; the rendering misses the sense of conceit.
problems.ruling: μέγα φρονεῖν is pride/conceit, not neutral 'think great things'; conceit versus small deeds is lost.

edits.old: It is terrible to think great things while doing small ones.
edits.new: It is terrible to think highly of oneself while doing small ones.

fixed: Fixed 'Having first known, know yourself' — προλαβὼν means 'beforehand/first', with no 'known' object; changed to 'First know yourself'.
Fixed 'to think great things' — μέγα φρονεῖν is the conceit idiom 'think highly of oneself', not thinking great thoughts.

last_rejected.why: Θεοσεβής means 'godly/pious,' not 'God-fearing' which implies fear.
last_rejected.fix: Godly is the one who does not speak on his own authority.
last_rejected.ruling: Θεοσεβής denotes reverence/piety; 'God-fearing' is a standard equivalent, not a meaning-changing error.

last_rejected.quote: does not speak on his own authority
last_rejected.why: κατά with the genitive (καθ' ἑαυτοῦ) means 'against himself,' not 'on his own authority' (which would be ἀφ' ἑαυτοῦ).
last_rejected.ruling: καθ' ἑαυτοῦ in this gnome means not from oneself, matching the English sense.

last_rejected.quote: It is terrible to think highly of oneself while doing small ones.
last_rejected.why: 'small ones' has no plural noun antecedent in the sentence; μικρά here means 'small things' or 'petty deeds.'
last_rejected.fix: It is terrible to think highly of oneself while doing small things.
last_rejected.ruling: μικρὰ πράττοντα is petty deeds; awkward English but meaning is clear.
